description: Deep-copy Django model instances with their related objects (one-to-many children, many-to-many links) using a declarative config and bulk_create.
rules: Import public names from the package root: from django_copyist import ModelCopyConfig, MakeCopy, TAKE_FROM_ORIGIN, TakeFromInput, UpdateToCopied, run_copy, check_config.
Run a copy with run_copy(config, input_data={...}). Check result.is_copy_successful before reading result.output_map.
Read copied primary keys with result.copies_of(Model). It returns {origin_pk: copy_pk}, both as strings.
Result maps are keyed by class name ('Company'). If two copied models share a class name, pass run_copy(..., map_keys=MapKeys.LABEL) to key them by 'app_label.ModelName'.
A root ModelCopyConfig needs filter_field_to_input_key, for example {'id': 'company_id'}, and input_data must contain that key.
Use MakeCopy(ModelCopyConfig(...)) only on reverse foreign keys (one-to-many accessors such as 'projects'). The child's FK to the copied parent is set automatically; do not list it.
Fields missing from field_copy_actions get their default value. List every field to keep with TAKE_FROM_ORIGIN.
A model that points to several copied parents goes into compound_copy_actions with UpdateToCopied(ParentModel) on each foreign key.
Validate every config in a test with check_config(config, raise_on_error=True). It runs no queries.
Generate a starting config with python manage.py copyist_scaffold app.Model --depth 2 after adding 'django_copyist' to INSTALLED_APPS.
Copies use bulk_create: save() and pre_save/post_save signals do not run. Use PostcopyStep for side effects.
Supported: Python 3.11+, Django 5.2/6.0/6.1, PostgreSQL, SQLite 3.35+, MariaDB (not tested in CI). MySQL and Oracle fail for auto-increment primary keys.
